ApostlesFast.description: The Church's oldest fast, kept by the apostles themselves after Pentecost: it begins the Monday after Pentecost and ends with the Feast of the Apostles on Abib 5, so its length follows the date of Easter, varying from 15 to 49 days. Fish is permitted.
ApostlesFast.title: Apostles' Fast

GreatFast.description: The holiest and greatest of the fasts: 55 days before the Resurrection, made of a preparation week, the holy Forty Days in the image of Christ's own fast in the wilderness, Lazarus Saturday and the Pascha week of His passion. A first-degree fast, kept until sunset, without fish.
GreatFast.title: Great Fast

NativityFast.description: Forty-three days before the Nativity, from Hatour 16: forty in the image of Moses' fast to receive the Word of God, kept now to receive the Word incarnate, and three added for the miracle of the Muqattam mountain in the days of Pope Abraam and St. Simon the Tanner. Through Kiahk, its nights fill with the special Kiahk praises.
NativityFast.title: Nativity Fast

NinevehFast.description: A three-day fast commemorating Nineveh's repentance at the preaching of Jonah, whose three days in the belly of the fish prefigure Christ's burial and Resurrection. Adopted from the Syrian church under Pope Abraam (10th century).
NinevehFast.title: Fast of Ninevah

StMaryFast.description: Fifteen days before the Assumption of the Virgin's body, Mesra 1 to 15. It is the fast most beloved of the Coptic faithful, whose devotion pressed the Church to adopt it formally.
StMaryFast.title: St. Mary's Fast
